To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found that the majority of neonates with extreme neonatal hyperbiliribinemia have a genetic basis for the hemolysis.
the most common genetic cause for extreme hyperbilirubinaemia is hereditary spherocylosis.
the causes of neonatal hyperbilirrubinemia are diverse and can be diagnosed with a combination of clinical, laboratory and genetic testing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to detect the hemolysis in the newborns.
the causes of neonatal hyperbilirrubinemia and the role of the bilirubin in the pathogenesis of the brain damage.
the development of new methods for the detection of hemolytic disease, and the development of a diagnostic algorithm for the detection of the most common forms of hemolytic anemia in neonates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of extreme hyperbilirubinaemia is associated with a high likelihood that there is an underlying cause for the jaundiced neonate, and that this cause is most likely to be a genetic haemolytic condition.
in neonates with TSB >25 mg dl1, the most common causes of hyperbilirubinemic jaundice are hereditary spherocytes, ABO incompatibility and G6PD deficiency.
a genetic basis for neonatal hemolysis can be found in 50% of neonates with extreme jaundice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the presence of extreme hyperbilirubinaemia, the first step should be a complete blood count, and a peripheral blood smear.
the presence of anemia, a positive DAT and a spherocyte population in the blood film should prompt consideration of an underlying genetic hemolytic condition.
a combination of clinical judgment and EMA flow cytometric analysis of erythrocytes is a cost-effective approach for the diagnosis of genetic causes of neonatal hemolytic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a systematic approach to the evaluation of extreme hyperbilirubinaemia is feasible, and can be used to improve the diagnosis and management of neonates with this condition.
the presence of a spherocytic red cell morphology on the peripheral smear is an important clue that a genetic erythrocyte disorder is likely.
the most important aspect of the evaluation is to have a high index of suspicion for a genetic hemolytic disease in neonates with severe jaundice.
